mission: Phase-4 data coverage, label latency & merchant history reconstruction

label_latency.label_1_meaning: Transaction flagged fraudulent at DATASET GENERATION time by the synthetic generator (pre-labeled static file)
label_latency.label_created_when: At dataset generation; there is no in-repo label-creation pipeline, investigation step, or confirmation timestamp (source: reports/data_provenance.json label_audit)
label_latency.labels_change_later: No mechanism in the dataset; static file (documented)
label_latency.label_availability_timestamp: ABSENT - no column or metadata records when a label would become available to a real-time scorer
label_latency.verdict: UNVERIFIED - the raw dataset cannot establish that a fraud label exists at the moment the model scores a later transaction
label_latency.generator_semantics: Fraud events are generated as bursts/archetypes; the generator assigns the label at transaction creation. In the synthetic world labels exist at t=0 for the CURRENT row and are usable for any LATER row by construction. Real-world confirmation delay cannot be inferred from the file.

empirical_exposure.interpretation: For each entity, the gap = time from an entity's fraud event to the NEXT transaction of that same entity. If labels lag by more than the gap, that next transaction is scored with a fraud-rate feature that does NOT yet include the fraud. User-level rates are the most latency-critical (median 0.22d, 90% within 1d); merchant rates need ~6.4d for half; city ~12.9d.

label_latency.train_vs_prod_finding: TRAINING fraud-rate features use an EXPANDING cumsum of ground-truth labels over the sampled stream; PRODUCTION uses a rolling 100-event window of decision-proxy labels (risk score>=70 recorded after each evaluation) with min_events=5 -> baseline 0.001. These differ in window, label source, and availability timing. The feature-parity certification compared the derive functions on the same context, NOT this tracker semantic.
label_latency.count_density_finding: Training count/velocity features were computed on 5%-sampled legit traffic; production tracks FULL traffic. Merchant coverage in training is the direct cause of the 'established-but-absent' FPR population (see merchant_coverage_matrix.json).

feature_inventory.training_definition: expanding mean of is_fraud over ALL prior rows of the user in the sampled chronological stream (shifted: the row itself never counts); baseline 0.001 before first row
feature_inventory.production_definition: EntityFraudRateTracker rolling window (last 100 events) fraction of CONFIRMED fraud events; min_events=5 else baseline 0.001; updated AFTER each evaluation from risk decision (score>=70 proxy) or DB-2 history
feature_inventory.notes: TRAIN/PROD SEMANTIC MISMATCH: training = expanding all-history cumsum of TRUE labels; production = rolling 100-window of DECISION-PROXY labels (score>=70) - a different quantity even with zero latency. Label availability at the exact scoring moment is UNVERIFIED.

feature_inventory.training_definition: expanding mean of is_fraud over ALL prior rows of the merchant (sampled stream, shifted)
feature_inventory.notes: same mismatch as user_fraud_rate. Merchant-level gap evidence: a fraud label would need to be available within median 6.4 days of the fraud for 50% of subsequent merchant scores to reflect it.

feature_inventory.training_definition: expanding mean of is_fraud over ALL prior rows of the merchant-city (sampled stream, shifted)
feature_inventory.notes: same mismatch. City-level gap: median 12.9 days.

feature_inventory.feature: user_tx_count / card_tx_count / merch_tx_count / user_avg_amt / amt_zscore / diversities / user_merch_count
feature_inventory.training_definition: expanding counts / means over prior SAMPLED rows (5% legit) of the entity (shifted)
feature_inventory.production_definition: velocity tracker / DB-2 real-time query counts over FULL live traffic (no sampling)
feature_inventory.notes: COUNT-DENSITY MISMATCH (coverage-related): training counts were computed on a 5%-legit sample; production counts full traffic. For a merchant with N true prior transactions, training sees ~N/20 - so training-level 'established merchant' signals are far weaker than production will feed.

feature_inventory.feature: all 6 merchant-establishment novelty features (merchant_age, is_merchant_new, merch_prior_rows, merch_prior_fraud, merch_prior_rate, merch_ever_seen_prior) [phase-2/3 candidates, NOT deployed]
feature_inventory.training_definition: full-corpus per-year aggregates strictly before the row's year (cumulative); merch_prior_fraud/rate use label counts
feature_inventory.production_definition: would require shipping the merchant table; label counts inherit the same availability question
feature_inventory.notes: leakage-audited PASS (future rows / own-year labels change nothing); label latency itself remains UNVERIFIED; merchant_age / prior ROWS are label-free and safe, prior FRAUD counts are label-dependent

label_latency.conclusion: LABEL LATENCY = UNVERIFIED (unchanged, per mission rules). Two actionable findings: (1) merchant_age + prior-row-count features are label-free establishment signals and are safe to add; (2) the production EntityFraudRateTracker feeds the model its OWN decisions as labels, so prod fraud-rate features are not the quantity the model was trained on - replacing that proxy with real confirmed labels (or dropping the three fraud-rate features) is the lowest-risk fix before any new model.

E_hardneg_val.note: top-bin over-predicts (0.36 vs 0.22) - ranking model, not calibrated probability, at high-risk end

absent.note: absent population severely miscalibrated (Brier 0.083 vs 0.007 seen). Ranking within the group is strong; absolute score level sits above the deployed threshold for ~77% of normal legit absent-merchant rows.

decision_matrix.question: Are labels available causally?
decision_matrix.finding: UNVERIFIED - no label-availability timestamp exists in the dataset; generator labels at transaction creation (t=0 for current, usable for later rows by construction).
decision_matrix.evidence: label_latency_audit.json; empirical exposure: user-level next-score median 0.22d after fraud, merchant 6.4d, city 12.9d.
decision_matrix.consequence: Label-dependent fraud-rate features (3 of 48) keep UNVERIFIED status; count-only establishment signals are safe.

decision_matrix.question: How much merchant coverage exists?
decision_matrix.finding: 24.4M rows / 63,288 name-hash merchant codes full corpus; 5% training pool covers 27,190 merchants (~47.0% of the 57,882 pre-2016 active).
decision_matrix.evidence: merchant_coverage_matrix.json (corrected name-hash universe; the earlier 98,138 came from a mis-hashed tuple volume table - see integrity note in the fix log).
decision_matrix.consequence: The 5% sampling rate is the distortion; ~53% of pre-2016-active merchants are absent from training.

decision_matrix.question: Are 'unseen' merchants actually new?
decision_matrix.finding: Mostly no - 87.8% of absent-merchant legit val rows are at established merchants (pre-2016 activity exists); 12.2% are genuinely new.
decision_matrix.evidence: cold-start taxonomy (A_truly_new 329 val rows vs B/C/D 2,146).
decision_matrix.consequence: Cold-start framing was mostly wrong; this is primarily a training-coverage artifact.

decision_matrix.question: Does greater coverage reduce FPR?
decision_matrix.finding: YES - absent@5-population FPR drops 0.667 -> 0.500 -> 0.448 (P1) as coverage rises 5% -> 10% -> 20%, while OVERALL FPR improves 0.067 -> 0.063 and recall stays >= 0.99.
decision_matrix.consequence: Primary cause = TRAINING COVERAGE, not model architecture (OUTCOME B - data redesign).

decision_matrix.question: Does establishment history help?
decision_matrix.finding: Partially - label-free establishment features (merchant_age, prior rows) are causal and validated; adding them improves absent FPR ~2-3 pts but costs ~1 pt overall (phase-2/3 frontier). Coverage itself is the larger lever.
decision_matrix.consequence: Track for the data redesign; not sufficient alone.

decision_matrix.question: Does calibration help?
decision_matrix.finding: No - E_hardneg is a ranking model; absent population is severely miscalibrated (Brier 0.083 vs 0.007) but ranking within group is good. Calibration is a symptom, not the cause.
decision_matrix.consequence: Do not pursue calibration as the fix; fix coverage.

decision_matrix.question: Is global threshold appropriate?
decision_matrix.finding: Subgroup analysis: flagged share at deployed threshold falls with history depth (0-hist 31.6% -> 21-200 9.8%) for seen merchants, but absent-code rows are flagged ~74-80% at ALL history depths. A single threshold is inappropriate across exposure regimes.
decision_matrix.consequence: Conditional thresholding is a candidate OUTPUT of the data redesign, not a standalone fix.

decision_matrix.question: Is another model justified?
decision_matrix.finding: Not yet - the gap is primarily training coverage (5% -> 20% halves absent FPR at equal-or-better overall performance). A new model trained on higher-coverage data is the right next step, but it must be validated independently before deployment.
decision_matrix.consequence: OUTCOME B: data/feature redesign recommended; E_hardneg stays deployed until the redesigned pipeline is independently certified.

verdict: OUTCOME B - DATA/FEATURE REDESIGN. E_hardneg remains deployed and untouched. The absent-merchant FPR is primarily a training-coverage artifact: 5% legit sampling omits ~53% of the 57,882 pre-2016-active merchants (87.8% of 'unseen' legit rows at established merchants, 12.2% genuinely new). Doubling coverage to 10-20% cuts the absent-population FPR from 0.667 to 0.448-0.500 with equal-or-better overall FPR and recall >= 0.99. Label latency remains UNVERIFIED; the production EntityFraudRateTracker feeds the model its own decisions as labels (score>=70 proxy) which is a different quantity than training's ground-truth expanding cumsum. INTEGRITY NOTE: universe counts in the original release (99,602/98,138 merchants) came from a mis-hashed (name,year)-tuple volume table; corrected to 63,288 name-hash codes / 57,882 pre-2016-active. Frame-derived coverage-simulation metrics are unaffected.
recommendation: KEEP E_hardneg deployed (control). Redesign the training data pipeline: (1) raise legit sampling / merchant coverage to >=20% (or merchant-aware sampling: keep all merchants with any fraud plus stratified legit coverage), (2) add label-free establishment features (merchant_age, prior row counts - already leakage-audited), (3) replace decision-proxy labels in EntityFraudRateTracker with confirmed feedback labels or drop the 3 fraud-rate features, (4) re-certify the redesigned candidate on the locked test only after validation. No production changes made in this mission. INTEGRITY: corrected merchant universe to 63,288 name-hash codes / 57,882 pre-2016-active (was 99,602/98,138 from a mis-hashed volume table).
